grh_46a51ac74a6d77ffc733.title: Babes in Toyland
paragraphs: Wicked Uncle Barnaby schemes against Alan and Jane and tries to force Mary into his own plans. grh_4625a4756d1de8a2d4ff.title: The Fugitive
paragraphs: An escaped prisoner in German uniform is shot near Rivers End on Christmas Eve, forcing Dr. Christian to decide whether wartime hatred can change a doctor's duty. He treats the wounded man and assists a mysterious visiting surgeon through a delicate operation, insisting that a patient must be cared for regardless of uniform. The apparent enemy is then identified as an American serviceman who had escaped a German prison camp wearing enemy clothing. The unknown surgeon departs before he can be thanked, while Dr. Christian concludes that the war may justify fighting the enemy's ideas but not abandoning a physician's obligation to an individual life.

The cast includes Jean Hersholt and Rosemary De Camp. Other credited names include Nelson Bond as writer and Bob Anderson as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 24 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_46543f52d33cf41a2dc1.title: Chicken Supreme
paragraphs: Dr. Christian receives an unwanted hen named Ella as payment from a poor patient and uses the odd gift while trying to help proud sisters Matilda and Lottie Tweedle find a useful occupation and a way to support themselves. At first the sisters intend to turn Ella into dinner, but failed attempts with a hatchet and then a shotgun leave them far too attached to the bird to kill her. Ella soon leads them into raising chicks, and what begins as sentiment becomes a serious poultry project. The women study feeding and breeding, rise early to care for the flock and devote themselves to building it properly. Their birds attract a buyer, and Christian helps them see how the operation can expand into a real business with more stock, runs, equipment and feed. The sisters gain work, independence and purpose. Their gratitude creates one last comic crisis when they decide the finest possible thank-you for Dr. Christian is to give him the best chicken in their flock, freshly killed.
This [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]] broadcast aired on April 10, 1940. It is listed as episode 75 in the archive.
The surviving recording runs about 24 minutes.

grh_465a96cb3895c286b245.title: The Queen Loved Herring
paragraphs: Nurse Nina Jones falls in love with wealthy Army Air Forces lieutenant Jimmy Bradley but is ashamed to let him meet the immigrant grandparents who raised her in their small delicatessen home. Jimmy's family has asked him to meet Nina's people before making a promise, and Nina becomes convinced that the contrast in background will end the romance. Dr. Christian sends Jimmy to the house anyway, where the grandparents welcome him with their own food, wine and traditions. To break Nina's obsession with pedigree, the doctor tells an elaborate story about disguised royalty whose queen prized an ordinary herring above jewels, then admits privately that the tale is nonsense that served a useful purpose. Jimmy sees the worth of Nina's family for himself, and he and Nina promise that when the bells of peace ring they will also be wedding bells.
